subject: ventures/time-off-request-planner
professional: a small-business operations manager / workforce scheduler (the kind who approves summer leave for a cafe, clinic or shop), with an operations-research reader as second: first checks are that no approved plan drops a role below the typed minimum on any working day, that the 'best plan' really is optimal for the stated objective, and that leave law and balances are not implied to be handled

evidence.correctness: `node --test` in the venture: 34 tests, 34 pass. Independent recomputation with my own Python 3 brute force (scratchpad ref.py: enumerates all 2^11 subsets of the built-in 11-request sample, uses datetime.date.weekday() for working days and my own per-role headcount-minus-minimum capacity, daily cap, blackout and same-person-same-day rules; not derived from calc.mjs) against solve() in calc.mjs. (1) Requests mode, Barista/Cook/Cashier minimums 2/2/1: optimum weight 20 with 7 approvals, set {2,3,4,6,7,9,10}; calc.mjs plan.score 20, same set. (2) Days mode: optimum 134, set {0,3,4,6,8,9,10}; calc.mjs plan.score 134, same set (and FCFS 115 vs 134 as shown). (3) Stress case: workdays Tue-Sat, cap 2 off per day, blackout 2026-07-20..21: optimum weight 13, set {0,2,4,9,10}; calc.mjs identical, and the working-day counts per request (9,9,4,6,4,5,4,4,9,4,9) are what Python's weekday gives for Tue-Sat. Also checked the date arithmetic: weekday(2026-07-06)=0 (Monday, correct), 2028-02-29 parses, 2/30/2026 rejected, Fri-Mon wraps to [Mon,Fri,Sat,Sun]. Denial reasons name the right first clash day and blockers (e.g. 2026-07-15 Wed, Cleo and Dev already off). Alternative windows were spot-checked by hand for Ana/Ben (2026-07-03..07-14: only Cleo overlaps at 1 of 4 baristas, fits). Tie-break by list order verified once by hand (B listed first wins, A denied). Not recomputed: the DOM rendering (no browser run) and the 3,000,000-node cut-off path beyond noting that a dense random 120-request/40-person case hit it (exact:false, nodes 3000001, 278 ms) and the code emits a warning that the plan is 'best found, not proven best'.
evidence.completeness: README/page claims walked: role minimums and N-M rule (works, tested); working-days spec and weekend-free requests (works); daily cap and blackouts (works, verified vs Python above); priority 1-5 default 3 with out-of-range error (works: 5.5 and 0 both rejected with the line number); maximise requests or days (both verified); exact branch and bound with brute-force comparison tests (calc.test.mjs:154, exists and passes); denial reason with first clashing day and who is off (works); nearest same-length window up to six weeks either side (42-day loop at calc.mjs:282, matches FAQ); FCFS comparison (counts and score reported); day-by-day cover calendar with 'tight' flag; both CSV exports with formula-injection defusing (test passes); CSV upload (index.html input#file exists and page.test.mjs checks every looked-up element exists); usage counting with opt-out. Limits are stated up front. Not seen: the page in a browser (not loaded here), so the click-through is taken from page.test.mjs structural checks. Gaps: the tool's own exported decisions CSV quotes cells containing commas but the request parser (splitLine) does not understand quotes, so a 'Smith, Jo' line is rejected (see defects); sitemap and robots point to relative URLs. No TODO stubs found in calc.mjs.
evidence.verification: Ran `node --test` in ventures/time-off-request-planner: tests 34, pass 34, fail 0 (0.35 s). Seeded three one-line mutations in calc.mjs, each followed by `node --test calc.test.mjs` and reverted with `git checkout` (git status clean for the venture afterwards): (a) capacity check `use + 1 > capOf[ri]` changed to `> capOf[ri] + 1` (lets one extra person be off than the minimum allows): 7 tests FAILED, caught. (b) isWork shifted by one weekday (`workdays.includes((weekday(d)+1)%7)`): 3 FAILED, caught. (c) tie-break `+ 500 - it.idx` changed to `+ 500 + it.idx` (ties would favour the request listed LAST, contradicting README 'then the request listed first'): 17 pass, 0 fail, NOT caught. The strong test is the exhaustive-subset comparison on random problems (calc.test.mjs:154), which compares optimal weight, not which of equally good sets is returned, hence the tie-break gap. Page tests are structural (disclaimer present, no fetch/XHR/beacon, labels, JSON-LD parse). The suite catches the safety-critical errors (cover violation) which is what a user would act on; the list-order tie rule is unpinned. Remaining unknowns: no browser/DOM test of the inline script, so rendering logic is only checked by import/element-existence tests.
evidence.craft: Read in full: calc.mjs (382 lines), usage.mjs, calc.test.mjs, page.test.mjs, index.html (markup, FAQ, script head). Good: pure functions, integer day numbers in UTC so no DST error, typed arrays for usage, deterministic, input limits (120 requests, 300 people, 800-day span, 3M node cap) with a user-visible warning when exact search is cut off, defensive localStorage handling, CSV formula defusing, HTML escaping helper on the page, no network. Defects: parseRequests/parsePeople split on commas with no quote handling, so quoted CSV fields (including this tool's own export, and any spreadsheet save of a name like "Smith, Jo") are rejected with a misleading 'dates must look like' error; role names are lower-cased for matching but cap lookup keys come from the first spelling (fine) while an unknown minimum role only warns; the +500 tie bonus can in principle outweigh a one-unit priority-days difference once 20+ extra approvals are involved (500 x 20 >= 10000), unlikely but not guarded or documented; sitemap.xml and robots.txt use relative URLs, which crawlers ignore; canonical is './index.html'. calc.mjs exports unused `money` helper (dead code). One 380-line file mixes parsing, solving and CSV; acceptable at this size.
evidence.claims: Checked: 'Nothing is uploaded / no network calls' backed by page.test.mjs:46-48 regex tests and by reading usage.mjs (localStorage counters only; I found no fetch/beacon). 'Exact branch and bound ... compared with brute force' backed by calc.test.mjs:154 and re-done by me above, BUT 'exact' is only true up to 3M nodes: my dense 120-request run hit the cap, and the README Model section says 'exact' without that qualifier (the page warns at runtime, the README does not). 'ties favour ... then the request listed first' is true in the code but unpinned by tests (mutation c survived). 'Deterministic': yes. 'Verified only against exhaustive search and invented data': honest and accurate. Disclaimer ('Not legal, tax, or financial advice', no warranty, best-effort hosting, not affiliated) present on index.html, README and llms.txt; the 'not modelled' list (statutory leave, notice, balances, sick leave) is explicit on page and README. VENTURE.yaml stage prototype, hypotheses untested, honest. Backed-but-wrong or unbacked: llms.txt links the tool at duncan-haywood.github.io, a host CLAUDE.md says now only redirects, while README and VENTURE.yaml use marisstella.app; sitemap.xml/robots.txt relative URLs do not do the SEO job the SEO checklist expects; README says 'node --test to run the tests' which works. README 'After using this, you can ... tell each person who is turned down which day clashes and which dates would work' is supported (reasons and alt windows verified).
evidence.fitness: Job walked through in code (not browser): a cafe manager with 9 staff and 11 requests pastes people, requests and minimums (the built-in sample is exactly this), gets 7 approved/4 denied, each denial carries the clashing day, who is off and an alternative window, plus a comparison with first come first served (score 20 vs 16 in requests mode, 134 vs 115 in days mode) and a cover calendar, and can export CSV. That is the job the page promises and the numbers are right. Friction a real manager would hit within the first hour: no quoted-CSV support (a spreadsheet export with 'Last, First' names fails), no per-person balance or carry-over (stated as not modelled), no way to lock an already-approved request in as a fixed constraint (the user can only emulate by high priority), and no saved plan between visits (by design). Priority is a manual 1-5 so fairness policy is the user's; fine and disclosed. No outside user yet (VENTURE.yaml untested, usage unmeasured).
evidence.domain: Compared against standard minimum-staffing leave approval practice and the optimisation formulation (weighted interval scheduling with per-role capacity constraints, an NP-hard multi-dimensional packing in general; exact B&B with an FCFS incumbent and a node cap is a sensible choice at this scale and I verified optimality against brute force on the sample and three variants). A workforce scheduler would accept the hard-rule model (headcount minus minimum per role per working day, daily cap, blackout) and would want exactly the disclosed exclusions (statutory leave, notice, accruals, skills/multi-role, part-time). Departures: weighting requests by an arbitrary 1-5 user priority is a policy tool rather than a fairness method (no seniority or rotation history built in, the page says to put policy in the priority column); alternative-window suggestion considers only same-length shifts and ignores a person's other pending requests; it does not model 'minimum per shift' within a day, which is stated.

defects.what: The list-order tie-break the README and FAQ promise ('ties favour more approvals, then the request listed first') is not pinned by any test: flipping `- it.idx` to `+ it.idx` leaves all 34 tests green, so which of several equally good plans a manager gets could change silently.

Request and people parsers split on commas without understanding quoted fields, so a spreadsheet-exported CSV with a name like "Smith, Jo", or this tool's own decisions CSV (which csvCell quotes), is rejected with the misleading message 'dates must look like 2026-07-06'. The page offers a 'requests CSV' upload, so this is the natural input path.

'Exact' search is exact only up to a 3,000,000-node cap. A dense random case (120 requests, 40 staff, two roles with minimums 15/15) hit the cap (exact:false, nodes 3000001). The page warns at run time, but README Model ('exact branch and bound') and VENTURE.yaml description ('exact search') state it without the qualifier.

sitemap.xml and robots.txt use relative URLs (`./index.html`, `Sitemap: ./sitemap.xml`); the sitemap protocol and robots.txt require absolute URLs, so crawlers ignore them. canonical is also './index.html'.
llms.txt points at the old duncan-haywood.github.io host, which now only redirects, instead of https://marisstella.app/time-off-request-planner/ used in README and VENTURE.yaml.

The +500 'more approvals' tie bonus (sum up to 60,000 over 120 requests) is not bounded below one priority unit (10,000), so with 20 or more extra approvals it could in principle outrank a real priority difference; unguarded and undocumented. Also `money` is exported but unused (dead code).

No browser-level test: the inline script's rendering (decisions table, calendar, CSV download) is checked only by import-name and element-existence tests, and I did not load the page, so UI behaviour is unverified in this audit.

verdict: A small, honest, correct prototype. Three independent brute-force recomputations in Python (requests mode, days mode, and a Tue-Sat / cap-2 / blackout case) agree exactly with calc.mjs on the optimal weight and the chosen set, date and weekday arithmetic is right, the 34 tests pass, and seeded mutations in the capacity check and the workday mapping were caught. It does not meet the bar only on claims: the tie-break rule it states is untested (a flipped sign survived all 34 tests), 'exact' is stated without the 3M-node qualifier (a dense 120-request case exceeded it), llms.txt links a stale host and sitemap/robots use relative URLs. Verification (3), correctness (3) and the median (3) meet the bar, claims (2) does not, so it does not meet the bar by the rubric; it is finished (completeness 3). The most user-relevant functional gap is quoted-CSV input, which rejects 'Last, First' names and the tool's own CSV export. The page was not loaded in a browser and the DOM script is only structurally tested.
